answer: A sybil defense ties reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than to account count. On a shared trellis, each agent must stake a slashable deposit and finish checkable tasks before its votes count; a newcomer that merely copies others cannot climb it. Like a raven known by its distinct call, an agent earns identity through consistent, useful behaviour, not by spawning clones. Rate limits and peer attestation then let a light zephyr of newcomers through while blocking floods of fakes, since duplicates share the same stake, history and failure pattern and are easy to discount.
